summary.intent: Avoid the per-request cost of urllib3's slow load_verify_locations() call for the common verify=True case by reusing one preloaded SSLContext across requests, instead of loading the CA bundle onto every connection pool anew.
summary.issue_fit: No originating issue; aligned against the caller-supplied PR title and body (spec-pr6667, https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/6667). The performance goal is met for the primary send()/_get_connection() request path; the accompanying claim that verify=True behaves exactly as before is only partial.
summary.coverage: Full merge-base diff (one file, src/requests/adapters.py, +28/-18) read at base and head; cert_verify(), _urllib3_request_context(), _get_connection(), and the still-public get_connection() extension point traced and cross-checked with direct read-only introspection against the pinned offline virtualenv (urllib3 2.8.0). Network-dependent tests are unavailable offline; a fresh-context worker independently confirmed the one security finding below.
check_details: Network-dependent ssl/verify pytest selection is unavailable offline; per the run policy, test_pyopenssl_redirect and test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert fail identically at merge-base and head ('Missing Authority Key Identifier', a fixture/OpenSSL-version mismatch), pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

Independent read-only introspection at the pinned head (offline venv, no network) showed get_connection() + cert_verify() leaves no CA trust source configured for verify=True (cert_reqs='CERT_REQUIRED', ca_certs=None, ca_cert_dir=None, no ssl_context), contrasted with the _get_connection() path, which correctly wires the preloaded SSLContext.

findings.title: Restore CA trust configuration for connections obtained via get_connection()
findings.trigger: A subclass overrides send() to call the older, still-public self.get_connection(url, proxies) -- kept specifically "without breaking things" per the comment above _get_connection() -- instead of self._get_connection(request, verify, ...), then calls self.cert_verify(conn, url, True, cert): the exact shape HTTPAdapter.send() itself used before _get_connection() existed.
findings.impact: The resulting pool has cert_reqs='CERT_REQUIRED' but ca_certs=None, ca_cert_dir=None, and no ssl_context, confirmed by direct introspection at the pinned head. urllib3's ssl_wrap_socket() then falls back to ssl.SSLContext.load_default_certs() (the OS trust store) instead of requests' pinned certifi bundle, or finds no usable certificates at all in a zip/frozen/minimal-CA environment -- precisely the scenario sigmavirus24 and tiran raised in review -- failing every HTTPS request through that adapter.
findings.change: In cert_verify() (src/requests/adapters.py), when verify is True, also set the CA trust source on conn directly (e.g. conn.ssl_context = _preloaded_ssl_context), so any conn is fully configured regardless of how it was obtained, restoring cert_verify()'s pre-change self-sufficiency.

requirements.evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:75-77,94-95 create a module-level _preloaded_ssl_context once at import and reuse it via pool_kwargs in the send()/_get_connection() path, avoiding a load_verify_locations() call per request for the common verify=True case.

requirements.source: spec-pr6667/pr-body/"If a verified connection is requested, _urllib3_request_context() already makes it so that a connection pool using a SSLContext with all relevant certificates loaded is always used."
requirements.evidence: Holds for the send()/_get_connection() path (traced and confirmed). Does not hold for connections obtained via the still-public get_connection() method (src/requests/adapters.py:406-433), which never receives the preloaded ssl_context -- see finding adapters/cert_verify-legacy-get_connection-ca-trust.

requirements.source: spec-pr6667/pr-body/"You can test against https://invalid.badssl.com to check that verify=True and verify=False still behave as expected and are now equally fast."
requirements.evidence: Network access is unavailable in this offline sandbox; live confirmation against invalid.badssl.com could not be performed. Static tracing supports the claim for the primary send()/_get_connection() path; it does not hold for the legacy get_connection() path (see above).
